findings.claim: TRUNK-6701 asks for three changes and this PR implements two; the third ("remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute") is untouched, and the evidence says it must stay, so the ticket's premise that nothing reads it needs correcting on the ticket rather than being left as an open half that a follow-up PR completes.
findings.evidence: Ticket (https://openmrs.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/TRUNK-6701) Requested change: 'Only write session attributes when their values actually change, and remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute.' The PR touches only username/locale; OpenmrsFilter.java:64 still does httpRequest.setAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID, String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis())). `git grep -n INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID` in the worktree at d381957e returns exactly two hits (WebConstants.java:20 definition, OpenmrsFilter.java:64 write) and no reader, with a positive control proving the pipeline works (`git grep -c WebConstants -- web/src/main` returns hits) -- so the ticket is right that core reads it nowhere. But it is a published contract: `gh api search/code -f q='INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID org:openmrs'` returns total_count=10, including openmrs-module-legacyui omod/.../taglib/HtmlIncludeTag.java and omod/.../controller/PortletController.java, openmrs-module-reporting ReportingPortletController.java, openmrs-module-htmlformflowsheet HtmlIncludeTag.java, openmrs-module-htmlwidgets HtmlUtil.java, openmrs-module-personalhr PortletController.java. Fetched legacyui HtmlIncludeTag.java: getInitialRequestUniqueId() (lines 153-170) reads pageRequest.getAttribute(WebConstants.INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID) and, when absent, log.error("Could not find value for ... in pageContext") and returns "", which collapses the per-request include de-duplication key to one empty-string bucket. The filter's own comment at line 63 ('used by htmlInclude tag') names that exact consumer and is accurate. 'Make it lazy' is also not available for a plain request attribute read via getAttribute, and String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis()) costs nothing worth optimising.

findings.claim: The class's @AfterEach logout() never logs anything out: the filter under test clears the thread's UserContext in its own finally block, so Context.logout() early-returns every time, making the cleanup dead code that reads as if it does something.
findings.evidence: Chain read in the tree at d381957e: OpenmrsFilter.java:114-116 `finally { Context.clearUserContext(); }`; Context.java:242-246 clearUserContext() -> userContextHolder.remove(); Context.java:970-972 isSessionOpen() -> userContextHolder.get() != null; Context.java:713-716 logout() -> `if (!isSessionOpen()) return;`. Verified empirically rather than read: I appended a temporary probe test to the class and ran `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest='OpenmrsFilterTest#zzProbe'`, which reported `entrySessionOpen=true|afterSessionOpen=false` -- the session is open when the test method starts and closed after doFilterInternal returns, so the @AfterEach is a no-op. Probe reverted (`git checkout --`), `git status --porcelain` clean. No behavioural harm: no base class declares a method named logout() (git grep 'void logout()' over api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/test and web/src/test/java/org/openmrs/web/test returns nothing, positive control: 25 'void ' hits in BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java), so this is a fresh method, not an override of base cleanup, and BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:937-945 re-opens the session in @BeforeEach. Full CI is green at this sha.

dimensions_swept.solution fit: Read TRUNK-6701 (summary, description, 1 comment) plus the PR body. The ticket's Background names three defects (anonymous username written then overwritten; locale re-written unchanged; an unread per-request unique-id attribute) and constrains session-creation behaviour as out of scope. Built the full truth table of base vs head over {userContext present/absent} x {authenticated/not} x {getUsername() null or not} and the end state is identical in every cell, including the null-username cell where both versions end with the attribute absent (setAttribute(name, null) removes it). httpRequest.getSession() at line 61 is byte-identical to base, so the out-of-scope constraint is honoured. Approach: weighed inlining the two comparisons without a helper (equivalent, duplicates the guard), promoting the guard to a public WebUtil helper (scope creep for two in-class call sites), dropping the attributes entirely and letting consumers read the UserContext (breaks the stated container-identification purpose and downstream readers), and wrapping the session in an HttpSessionWrapper that swallows no-op writes (affects every attribute, wrong size). The private per-attribute helper is the proportionate choice, so nothing to raise on approach. Hunk accounting: the Objects import, the username-computation restructure, the test and the dataset are all required by the ticket or its acceptance criteria; `git diff --ignore-all-space --stat` is byte-identical to the plain --stat, so there is no whitespace or format-on-save churn, and there are no drive-by hunks. Only gap is A1 -- two of the three requested changes done.
dimensions_swept.correctness: Read both full versions of OpenmrsFilter.java (base eda229b1 and head d381957e), not just the hunks. Confirmed UserContext.getAuthenticatedUser() (UserContext.java:211-213) is a bare field read, so hoisting it out of the removed else branch and calling it on a freshly constructed UserContext is side-effect-free and returns null there, preserving the anonymous default. UserContext.getLocale() (UserContext.java:349-356) falls back to LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale() when unset, and is called identically in both versions. Objects.equals is the right comparison for String and the immutable Locale. Read-then-write is not atomic, but concurrent requests on one session write the same value from the same UserContext, and base wrote unconditionally anyway. A skipped write can only happen when the stored value already equals the value that would be written, so a stale replica cannot pin a wrong username. An invalidated session throws IllegalStateException from getAttribute where base threw it from setAttribute -- same failure at the same point. Empirically: `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` is 5/5 green at the head sha.
dimensions_swept.test coverage: Ran the falsification experiment rather than reading the assertions: checked the base OpenmrsFilter.java into the worktree, re-ran OpenmrsFilterTest, got 3 failures / 5 -- shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAnonymousSessionAttributes (expected 0, was 1), shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticatedSessionAttributes (expected 0, was 2), shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale (expected 1, was 2, i.e. the intermediate anonymous write the PR description claims to eliminate) -- then restored the file and confirmed 5/5 green. So the tests assert the runtime effect (setAttribute call counts on a recording session), fail on base and pass on head. shouldSetAnonymousUsernameAndLocale and shouldUpdateChangedSessionAttributes pass on base; they are value-regression tests guarding the 'same values as today' criterion, which is a legitimate role. Probed the locale discrimination: the default locale under test is en_GB, so Locale.ENGLISH in shouldUpdateChangedSessionAttributes genuinely differs and the assertion is meaningful (and would fail loudly, not silently, if that ever changed). Uncovered: only-one-of-the-two-attributes-changed, and the null-getUsername() path; both are pre-existing or trivially independent, so neither is worth a comment. A2 is the one test-side finding.
dimensions_swept.security: No secrets, no CI config, no deserialization, no injection surface, no authorization decision in the diff. The username/locale session attributes carry no new information and end with the same values as before, so nothing is newly exposed to a session reader. Confirmed nothing in the repo consumes the write *events* that the PR now suppresses: `git grep HttpSessionAttributeListener|attributeReplaced|attributeAdded|HttpSessionBindingListener` over the whole tree returns nothing (positive control: `git grep -c HttpSession -- web/src/main` returns hits in Listener.java, CookieClearingFilter.java, OpenmrsFilter.java), and Listener.java:78-185 only fans sessionCreated/sessionDestroyed out to Spring-registered HttpSessionListener beans, which attribute writes never reach. The bound values are String and Locale, neither of which implements HttpSessionBindingListener.
dimensions_swept.performance: This is the PR's purpose, and it delivers: the steady state goes from 2-3 session attribute writes per request to 0, at the cost of 2 getAttribute reads. For a replicating manager that is the difference between recording a delta (or marking the attribute dirty for a Redis-backed store) and a map lookup, which is the mechanism the ticket names. Measured as call counts by the tests themselves (0 writes on an unchanged repeat request, 1 instead of 2 on an authenticated request). Nothing is added to a loop, no query is introduced, and LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale() was already being reached once per request through userContext.getLocale() in the base version, so there is no new per-request global-property read.
dimensions_swept.project conventions: Import ordering follows the java.* -> jakarta.* -> org.* grouping already in the file, and java.util.Objects sorts correctly after java.io.IOException. Checked the jspecify @NonNull in the test override against project history instead of flagging it: 9 files use jspecify, including web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/GZIPFilter.java in the very same package, so it is established here. The test lives beside CookieClearingFilterTest/GZIPFilterTest in web/src/test/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/ and extends BaseWebContextSensitiveTest like the other five subclasses in the module. Mixed hamcrest assertThat and JUnit assertEquals in one class is the only stylistic divergence from the other assertThat-using web tests, and it is purposeful (values vs long counts) with a clean Sonar gate, so I am not reporting it. A3 is the convention finding worth raising.

All work in the prepared worktree at d381957e; `git status --porcelain` is empty at hand-off (I mutated two files for evidence -- checked the base OpenmrsFilter.java in for the falsification run, and appended a probe test for the lifecycle facts -- and restored both with git checkout, noting that after `git checkout <sha> -- <path>` the index also has to be reset or `git checkout -- <path>` restores the base version again; I hit that and fixed it). Verdict: nothing blocking. The change is behaviour-preserving on end state in every case I could construct, it is the proportionate fix, and its tests fail on base and pass on head; A1 is the comment with real value, because it is about the ticket being wrong rather than the code.
